advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the exact-prose substring assertions in test_t15_deployed_service_fast_proof_fixture_carries_the_full_contract with structural checks (e.g. the fixture's `expect`/`mode`/`criterion` fields) so a behavior-preserving reword of the fixture prose does not break the test.
evidence:
"for proof_contract in (
        "out-of-loop",
        "before codifying",
        "minutes",
        "only resources created by this experiment",
    ):
        assert proof_contract in text" (tests/unit/test_t15_overlay_derisk_criterion.py:109-115)

The asserted strings live in the fixture's `input:` prose, which is consumed by the model at eval time, not by a parser that branches on the exact substring — an LLM is not a non-human consumer under Rule-5.
Litmus (Rule 4): rewording the fixture prose while preserving its meaning would fail this test with no observable-behavior change, so it is a change-detector.
advisory.finding: test_t15_deployed_service_fast_proof_fixture_carries_the_full_contract asserts exact prose phrases inside the model-input fixture ('out-of-loop', 'before codifying', 'minutes', 'only resources created by this experiment'). These are natural-language prompt text fed to an LLM, not tokens parsed by a non-human consumer; a behavior-preserving reword of the fixture (e.g. 'resources this experiment created') breaks the test without any change to what the corpus tests. This is a change-detector on the author's wording rather than a verifier of observable eval behavior.
